item.title: Who will replace Rishabh Pant? Ex-India opener reveals LSG's two leading captaincy options
item.description: Lucknow Super Giants' decision to bring Kuldeep Yadav on board through a trade could prove to be one of their most influential moves ahead of IPL 2027, according to former India opener Abhinav Mukund. He believes the left-arm wrist-spinner has the ability to transform LSG's bowling attack and potentially play a decisive role in their pursuit of a maiden IPL title. Kuldeep joined LSG shortly after the conclusion of IPL 2026, with the franchise completing a trade deal with Delhi Capitals that saw wicketkeeper-batter Rishabh Pant move in the opposite direction. Mukund believes Kuldeep's wicket-taking ability makes him an invaluable addition, particularly at the Ekana Stadium, where conditions are expected to assist spin bowling. He also highlighted the prospect of Kuldeep forming an attacking partnership with fellow spinner Digvesh Rathi. “Kuldeep Yadav is a phenomenal signing for Lucknow Super Giants. He is a genuine wicket-taking spinner, and in T20 cricket, that is worth its weight in gold. “He does not just keep the runs down, he looks for wickets in the middle overs, and that changes the game for a captain. At the Ekana Stadium, where the pitch offers help to spinners, he will be even more dangerous. His partnership with Digvesh Rathi could be one of the most exciting spin pairings in the IPL. “Both of them are attacking bowlers who are not afraid to toss the ball up and invite the batters to go after them, because they know their variations can get them out. When you have two spinners asking different questions, it becomes very hard for the opposition to settle. If they build a strong understanding, LSG will have a spin attack that can win them games on its own and for me, this trade could be one of the smartest moves of the season,” Mukund told JioStar. However, while Kuldeep's arrival strengthens the bowling department, LSG still have an important decision to make regarding their leadership. Pant's exit has left the franchise searching for a new captain as they prepare for another attempt at winning their first IPL trophy. Mukund identified Aiden Markram and Nicholas Pooran as the two leading candidates currently available within the squad. Both have experience captaining franchise teams in different T20 leagues. However, he believes LSG could also explore the possibility of bringing in an experienced Indian player through the trade window. “Lucknow Super Giants are on the hunt for a captain. Now it depends on their team management about what they prefer, whether they prefer to appoint a captain from a player in their squad or whether they choose someone from the mini auction. The strongest option within the squad is Aiden Markram. “He leads their SA20 side, Durban’s Super Giants, which makes his case for leading LSG quite strong. Referee Damian Schneider, in consultation with television match official (TMO) Marius van der Westhuizen, quickly deemed that the incident met the yellow card threshold, with foul play review officer Aled Griffiths upgrading the sanction to a 20-minute red card. The challenge was deemed to be a high degree of danger with no mitigation. Under World Rugby rules, Japan are permitted to replace Hockings after that 20-minute period has elapsed. But what are the laws around head contact that referees are following and how do they decide on the punishment? Here’s everything you need to know: What are World Rugby’s laws on head contact? Head-on-head contact in the tackle comes under Law 9 of the Laws of Rugby Union , which covers foul play. Law 9.11 dictates “Players must not do anything that is reckless or dangerous to others, including leading with the elbow or forearm, or jumping into, or over, a tackler” and Law 9.13 goes on to say “A player must not tackle an opponent early, late or dangerously. Dangerous tackling includes, but is not limited to, tackling or attempting to tackle an opponent above the line of the shoulders even if the tackle starts below the line of the shoulders.” If a player breaks these laws and the act is deemed to be reckless or dangerous, then the referee is entitled to issue a yellow or red card. World Rugby also clarify the intent of the laws, stating in their guidelines that: “Player welfare drives World Rugby ’s decision making for zero tolerance of foul play, especially where head contact occurs. If any head contact is made at all, we move on to Step 2. Step 2 (was there foul play?) is a touch more complex. item.title: Magnificent Wales end 73-year New Zealand hoodoo
item.description: Nations Championship Wales (21) 35 Tries: T Williams, Lake, Griffin, James, Rees-Zammit Cons: Costelow 5 New Zealand (21) 28 Tries: Ratima, Sititi, Fineanganofo, Lakai Cons: Mo'unga 4. Wales celebrated a first victory against New Zealand in 73 years with a brilliant performance to spark astonishing scenes in Cardiff. Steve Tandy's unfancied side lifted a nation as they broke a 34-match losing sequence against the All Blacks that stretched back to 1953. In a nine-try Nations Championship thriller at the Principality Stadium, Wales led 14-0, 21-7 and 35-21 before they held off New Zealand with a wonderful defensive display in the final quarter, led by flankers James Botham and Jac Morgan and lock Dafydd Jenkins. The home side produced a stunning start with tries from inspirational scrum-half Tomos Williams and captain Dewi Lake inside the first six minutes. Prop Archie Griffin also added a first-half try, but New Zealand responded with scores from scrum-half Cortez Ratima, number eight Wallace Sititi and wing Fehi Fineanganofo to level the score 21-21 at half-time. Wales centre Eddie James and wing Louis Rees-Zammit scored early second-half tries before New Zealand flanker Peter Lakai pulled one back. The remarkable Wales defence followed as they held up the All Blacks three times over the line to stop New Zealand scoring, to evoke wild celebrations. Good things come to those who wait Wales had won the first three games in this fixture in 1905, 1935 and 1953 but have had to wait more than seven decades for the next. In 1953 the New Zealand dollar did not exist, Cardiff was not the capital city of Wales and tries were only worth three points. Sections of the New Zealand media had belittled Welsh rugby before the game, while some bookmakers offered odds of 20-1 for a Wales victory. Legends such as Sir Gareth Edwards, Alun Wyn Jones, Shane Williams, JPR Williams, Barry John and Phil Bennett had never enjoyed success against New Zealand in a Welsh jersey. Now Tandy's class of 2026 have written their own chapter in Welsh rugby's history. The 55,152 was the lowest crowd in the 14 matches between Wales and New Zealand at the Principality Stadium. The fans who stayed away will regret it because it was a day to say "I was there". Welsh rugby has been in the doldrums for so long, on and off the field, but will hope this famous victory can help galvanise the nation. This was one of the finest performances in Welsh rugby history and a world apart from the display in the 28-21 win against Japan last weekend. New Zealand might regret failing to take advantage of France's victory against South Africa on Friday night but they still leapfrog the Springboks to top the southern section with one weekend of regular matches remaining. item.description: The Kansas City Chiefs are expected to play Sunday’s NFL Week 10 game at the Atlanta Falcons without running back Kenneth Walker III , the engine behind the reigning Super Bowl champions’ 6-2 start. Kansas City will hold Walker out with a groin injury, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, who reported that the Chiefs “want to give him a week,” per a source. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport added that Sunday’s game was “ too quick of a turnaround ” for the Chiefs’ workhorse. Walker has 872 rushing yards, eight behind Falcons star Bijan Robinson for the NFL lead despite playing one fewer game, and his 11 scrimmage touchdowns tie Jahmyr Gibbs for the most in the league. Schefter reported he hurt his groin in Thursday’s practice. item.title: Grand Slam of Darts: Schedule, results & prize money
item.description: Luke Littler became world number one for the first time when he won the Grand Slam of Darts in 2025 [Press Association] The 2026 Grand Slam of Darts gets under way on Saturday, as another of the Professional Darts Corporation's (PDC) major titles is set to be won in Wolverhampton. This edition is bigger than ever, with 48 players taking part, and unlike most of darts' major tournaments, the players are split into groups in the initial phase, rather than a straight knockout format. Each player will face two opponents in their group, with only the group winner progressing into the last 16. The rest of the competition is a straight knockout format. Luke Littler is the defending champion following a 16-11 victory over Luke Humphries in the 2025 final to become world number one for the first time. Littler faces a tough start, with Beau Greaves his opponent on the opening evening, and Neils Zonneveld, who beat Littler in their only previous meeting, completing the group. When is the Grand Slam of Darts? The tournament lasts for nine days from Saturday, 14 November to Sunday, 22 November. Group stage (14-17 November) - 48 matches Second round (18-19 November) - eight matches Quarter-finals (20-21 November) Semi-finals (22 November) Final (22 November) What is the format? In the group stage, the format is best of nine legs, or first to five legs. In the initial phase, two points are awarded for a win, with the group winner progressing to the last 16. In case of players being level on points at the end of the group phase, the following tie-breakers apply: Total Leg Difference Total Legs Won Total Legs Won Against Throw Highest Total Tournament Average (to two decimal places) Highest Winning Match Average (to two decimal places) A play-off - nine-dart leg Second-round matches are a best-of-19 format, or first to 10 legs. The quarter-finals, semi-finals and final are best of 31 legs, or first to 16 legs. Who is playing and how did they qualify? With the tournament expanded, a new set of qualification rules have been put in place. Up to 24 players could qualify from reaching a major PDC televised final in the past 12 months, but only nine ended up qualifying via that route, partly because of the dominance Littler has shown. Ten players reached Wolverhampton from the PDC youth, development and challenge tours, the Women's Matchplay and Women's Series and championships from across the globe. Six more secured places through the European Tour, while 13 qualified with a Players Championship win. The final 10 spots, which include ninth seed Stephen Bunting, were claimed in a PDC tour card holder qualifying event. From there, the top-16 ranked players in the PDC's order of merit were seeded and filled pot one. The next 16 went into pot two and the final 16 made up pot three. One player from each pot was then allocated to a group. Grand Slam of Darts groups, order of play & results Afternoon sessions start at 13:00 GMT, with evening sessions at 19:00 (19:30 on 15).

item.description: On what ended up being an excellent day for Sonia Bompastor , the Chelsea manager first had to accept that it started with a mistake. Kadeisha Buchanan, the centre-back, had been cleared to start by Chelsea’s medical team despite taking a knock to the head in training on Friday. Her assignment was to stop the world’s best striker, Khadija Shaw , who had arrived at Stamford Bridge having scored in nine Women’s Super League games in a row since the start of the season. But the way Chelsea set up in their top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City at first appeared designed to present Shaw with every opportunity to make it 10. For Bompastor, it soon became apparent that something was not right. Buchanan, visibly struggling, was given a torrid opening 12 minutes, beaten for pace by Shaw twice on the outside and dragged into deeply uncomfortable positions as the striker roamed and bared her teeth. Aoba Fujino should have fired the champions in front after four minutes, but she placed Shaw’s cut-back horribly wide after Buchanan had been easily by-passed. Katie McCabe then had a narrow escape when she sliced Shaw’s cross past the post. Bracing herself on the touchline, Bompastor had to act. The Chelsea back-line all looked up with the same blank expression as Veerle Buurman stood ready on the sideline; no one appeared to know the change that was coming. Buchanan, perhaps to hide her embarrassment, went straight down the tunnel. “Watching her from the beginning of the game, she was not 100 per cent,” Bompastor explained. “I know my player and she was not in the game. You have to be brave to make that change in the moment.” Bompastor made three changes before the start of the second half but they all strengthened Chelsea (Reuters) Changing her back-line that early, Bompastor said, was a “risk”, but it was the ruthless change Chelsea needed. Bompastor spent the first half tinkering and tweaking until they could feel as if they could go toe-to-toe with Andree Jeglertz’s side. By the start of the second half, Chelsea had already made three changes. Buchanan’s early withdrawal was followed by Melvine Mallard being forced off with a hamstring injury. Sandy Baltimore’s stunning strike ended up being the winner, a thunderbolt that even she did not seem to expect judging by the forward’s nonchalant celebration, but it was also her final touch as she was replaced at the break, as Bompastor decided to make a half-time change instead of using up her only available substitute window early in the second half. item.title: LSU Star Blames Ole Miss Coaches For Pressure, Cites “Unclean Hands”
item.description: John Reed-Imagn Images Two former Ole Miss players now on the LSU roster are fighting a combined $950,000 buyout demand. Princewill Umanmielen and Devin Harper claim their old coaches used unfair pressure to get them to sign contracts they later broke. Their legal filings argue the university cannot collect money because of how the deals were made. According to EssentiallySports , the players’ defense states that “Ole Miss has unclean hands” and is entitled to no relief. The dispute centers on revenue-sharing agreements signed in early January 2026. Umanmielen signed on January 3, and Harper signed three days later. Both deals included a 90-day early-termination clause. If the players left voluntarily within that window, they owed specific payments. Umanmielen faces a $550,000 claim, while Harper faces a $400,000 claim. Both men transferred to LSU in January after head coach Lane Kiffin moved there. They left Ole Miss within the 90-day window, triggering the buyout terms. Players Claim Coaches Used Undue Pressure The legal battle has shifted focus from the players leaving to how the contracts were signed. Umanmielen argues he signed his deal under “undue pressure” from Ole Miss coaches . The lawsuit filed by Ole Miss led him to doubt that he would receive a fair trial in Oxford. Mauricio Pochettino to ban players’ day off after games According to The Sun , Pochettino is set to “crack the whip” with his players to improve their much-criticised fitness. When the Vikings called San Francisco as part of due diligence in their search for a quarterback, sources told ESPN that Niners general manager John Lynch informed Minnesota brass that it would take a second-round pick and more for Jones. Perhaps a second-rounder and a middle-round pick might have gotten a trade done. Instead, because of the high cost associated with the veteran quarterback, the conversations ended there and Jones remains a valued member of the 49ers. This was not the first time the teams had spoken about Jones in a possible trade and not the first time San Francisco had set a price that high. Niners coach Kyle Shanahan views Jones as a franchise-caliber quarterback and would trade him only for a deal they had no choice but to accept. To add to that value, Jones won four of his first five starts in place of the injured Brock Purdy last year despite battling injuries of his own and ended up with a 5-3 record and a QB rating of 97.4 for the season. In the final year of his two-year, $8.41 million contract, Jones is a free agent after the season. The 49ers must feel pretty confident that Jones will sign a big enough contract this offseason to net the team at least a third-round compensatory pick. If you’re the 49ers, it’s wise to make a team you could face in the playoffs overpay for a quarterback. It might have been a different story if another team had inquired about Jones. Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert was on the 49ers’ radar: While the Eagles traded stars in Davis and center Cam Jurgens in the flurry leading up to the deadline, they held off trading another player who was wanted — Dallas Goedert . Sources said several teams inquired about the pass-catching tight end, including the 49ers. But Goedert, 31, never got close to being traded. He remains in Philadelphia and could even re-sign with the Eagles for 2027. Goedert has lined up as an inline tight end 48.7% of the time this year, compared to 38.1% in the slot. I think these moves tell us the 49ers were looking to get another big body to pair with George Kittle, who they can throw the ball to. item.description: Controversy over Raphinha as Brazil refuses to release Barcelona superstar – report Earlier today, it seemed Barcelona were set for a massive boost following Raphinha’s red card incident against Japan in a friendly. The forward received a red card for protesting after Japan’s late winner, which means he was immediately ruled out for the next friendly against Singapore. This led many outlets to report that Brazil is now considering releasing Raphinha and allowing him to return to Barcelona, since he won’t be available against Singapore anyway. Brazil refuses to release Raphinha Raphinha received a red card against Japan. (Photo by Ashok Kumar/Getty Images) However, in what would be a highly controversial move, it appears Brazil has no desire to release Raphinha early, in spite of his unavailability against Singapore. This was confirmed by Rodrigo Caetano, chief executive officer of Brazilian football federation, who told the media that the team does not wish to release Raphinha. “Raphinha stays. In principle, he stays with us. It does not make sense (to leave), because he is one of our leaders, ” he said (h/t Diario SPORT ). This is a blatant violation of the unwritten and unsaid understanding that national teams and clubs have always had, since there are many precedents in the past where a player was allowed to leave early if he was deemed unavailable for the next match. A grave concern for Barcelona Raphina won’t be allowed to leave the Barcelona camp. (Photo by Ashok Kumar/Getty Images) This is not the best of news for Barcelona, as Raphinha will now only run the risk of potentially picking up an injury while training with the national team in Singapore, but also potentially failing to be fully fit and available for the game against Villarreal. It must be noted that Brazil are slated to take on Singapore on Tuesday. Raphinha will be allowed to return to the Barcelona camp only after the game. The distance between Singapore and Barcelona is roughly 11,000 km, making it a long and tedious journey for Raphinha, who will then have to rest up and get back to full fitness by the time Barcelona take on Villarreal on Sunday. While that doesn’t necessarily mean Raphinha won’t be available against Villarreal, it does make things significantly difficult for the Barcelona star, who would have preferred to return to Ciutat Esportiva immediately.

item.title: Nations Championship schedule, results, kick-off times and how to watch
item.description: Rugby’s Nations Championship bursts back into life as the inaugural edition comes to a conclusion in a busy November. The new competition pits the Six Nations sides against the four Rugby Championship competitors, plus Japan and Fiji, across six matches split evenly across the July and November Test windows. The results of those games will determine each of the 12 teams’ seedings for the finals weekend at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium , with six matches contested over two days and both team and hemisphere silverware up for grabs. Each entrant will be matched against the equivalent qualifier from the other pool to decide overall placings at the conclusion of a busy year of international action. South Africa and New Zealand are assured of a top-two finish in their pool – with the All Blacks failing to take a huge opportunity to seize the initiative after the Springboks were beaten by France as Wales made history in Cardiff. Here’s the full competition schedule, and how it will all work: What is the Nations Championship? Announced during the 2023 Rugby World Cup, the new competition will be held every other year and replaces the traditional summer tours and Autumn Nations Series. It is designed to add context to the international calendar, with Fiji and Japan invited to join the Six Nations and Rugby Championship sides to form a top 12. Promotion and relegation is planned for the future with the second-tier Nations Cup, though will not take place in 2026. The entrants are: Northern Hemisphere : France, Ireland, Scotland, Italy, England, Wales. Southern Hemisphere: South Africa, New Zealand, Argentina, Australia, Fiji, Japan. item.title: Mets Target Ty France After Career Year With Padres
item.description: San Diego Padres first baseman Ty France (25) hits an RBI single during the seventh inning of their National League Division Series game against the Milwaukee Brewers Sunday, October 4, 2026 at American Family Field in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. The New York Mets need a fix at first base, and they have found a clear target in Ty France . After a season where their hitters at the position finished dead last in fWAR, the front office is looking to add a proven bat. MLB reporter Michael Marino confirmed the move on X.com, stating, “Sources: The Mets have shown interest in free-agent first baseman Ty France as they look to bolster the position.” This interest comes right after France posted his best numbers ever with the San Diego Padres. Sources: The Mets have shown interest in free-agent first baseman Ty France as they look to bolster the position. France joins Alec Bohm as one of the 1B’s drawing the teams attention. — Michael Marino (@MarinoMLB) November 13, 2026 A Career Year for France France is 31 years old and just finished a campaign that defined his career. He hit 21 home runs, which was a new personal best, and added 24 doubles in 133 games. His 4.5 bWAR was also the highest mark of his time in the majors. In 2026, the Mets realized their first base unit performed poorly, as the group finished with an 85 wRC+, placing just ahead of the last-place Diamondbacks. Matt Carroll of JustBaseball.com observed that the production deficit extended beyond hitting to include fielding, where the unit tied for second-to-last in fielding run value. Signing France would give the Mets a thumping run-producer. The team lost Pete Alonso in free agency, leaving a massive hole that has yet to be filled. France joins Alec Bohm as a top option , but the Padres star offers a different skill set. Marino wrote that “France joins Alec Bohm as one of the 1B’s drawing the team’s attention.” The Mets have been looking at Bohm too, but France might be the cheaper route to a solid lineup spot. Why France Fits the Plan France’s 139 OPS+ is the best of his career, showing he can handle major league pitching. While he had some rough years before, this past season proved he is ready for a big role. With the Mets pursuing first base assistance this offseason, their pursuit of France is hardly unexpected. Since Jake Bauers reportedly agreed to a $58 million, four-year contract with the Boston Red Sox, France stands as the next-best available first baseman. His 72 RBI and .865 OPS show he can drive in runs and get on base. The danger is genuine given that he recorded only 0.4 bWAR over 278 games during the prior two seasons. Nevertheless, his upside is compelling enough that the Mets might secure him through a sensible multi-year agreement without overspending. The front office knows they need a player who can hit, and France has shown he can do just that. item.title: Tenerife boss says Owono's 12-match ban 'feels light'
item.description: Alvaro Cervera has been Tenerife manager since 2024 [Getty Images] Tenerife manager Alvaro Cervera says that goalkeeper Jesus Owono's 12-match ban "might feel light" but he accepts that the regulations do not "specifically account for what happened". FC Andorra's Owono, 25, was sent off after colliding with Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel during the closing stages of the Spanish second-tier match between their two respective sides on 2 November. De Miguel died the following day aged 30, and a disciplinary committee from the Spanish football federation confirmed Owono's suspension on Friday. It was the maximum punishment that he could have received as the disciplinary committee could only consider the offence on the pitch and not "the tragic outcome of the incident". "I think that, just as in other areas of life, there are rules or laws that must be followed," said Cervera, speaking before his club's fixture against Ceuta on Sunday - their first match since De Miguel's death. "Since the current regulations don't specifically account for what happened, I believe they have simply adhered to the rules and imposed the number of matches permitted by the regulations. "Anything else I might say would just be my own personal opinion, which I'll keep to myself. It might seem a bit light when compared to other cases, but in reality, I don't think the rules allow for anything else." The disciplinary committee also said it had to base its decision "on the facts expressly recorded in the referee's report", which stated the player "was sent off for 'violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play'". 'Normality isn't something you'll find right now' Cervera, 61, also described the experience of returning to training and preparing for their next match as "tough" and "complicated". "When we're together, we're fine, during our sessions, we're doing well," he said. "It feels like the group is gradually getting back to normal. What we don't know is how everyone is doing when we're apart and that's a significant factor. "Everyone has their own way of coping and their own thoughts; some have people at home to support them, while others are more on their own. "We're making progress, a very slow process, but we are moving forward - it's tough, it's complicated." He also said that he was not sure whether his players were ready to return to playing, describing how some would appreciate a distraction and others will not be in the right frame of mind yet. "Both positions are reasonable," Cervera added. "On one hand, you want to return to some sense of normality though you know that true normality isn't something you'll find right now. "This isn't something you can just set aside or push to the back of your mind to focus on your own work; it's not like other life events you might encounter. item.description: Motorsport photo When Lewis Hamilton joined Nico Rosberg at Mercedes for the 2013 Formula 1 season, it was a feel-good story: two long-time friends becoming team-mates. item.title: How Fernando Mendoza could make NFL history vs Mike Macdonald’s Seattle Seahawks
item.description: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images Fernando Mendoza will make his first-ever start in the NFL for the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks. Amid the excitement of making his debut start, there will surely be some nerves for the 22-year-old, as he prepares to go up against the reigning Super Bowl champions. This Seattle defense has even earned the ‘Dark Side’ nickname – that’s how good they have been over the last 12 months. The Raiders have not exactly been firing on all cylinders since the opening three games of the season. Following their three-game winning start to the year, Klint Kubiak’s team have gone 1-5 in their following six games. History will be against Mendoza on Sunday, with quarterbacks making their debut against a Mike Macdonald defense not faring very well. Fernando Mendoza could write his name in NFL history by beating the Seattle Seahawks Mendoza has already taken some snaps in the NFL, following his cameo appearance in the emphatic defeat against the New England Patriots last month. Taking snaps in a game where the result has already been decided is one thing, but being in from the start is a totally different prospect. ESPN’s beat reporter for the Seahawks, Brady Henderson, shared a statistic showing how debutant quarterbacks have fared against Macdonald’s Seahawks. Mendoza will be the fifth quarterback to make his starting debut against Seattle since Macdonald was hired as the head coach. Bo Nix [Denver], Caleb Williams [Chicago], Cam Ward [Tennessee] and Max Brosmer [Minnesota] have all made their debuts against the Seahawks since 2024, yet none of them came out victorious against Macdonald’s defense. It was only Ward who was able to even throw a touchdown against the Seahawks in those games, with seven interceptions being thrown by the other three quarterbacks in the list. Mendoza has the opportunity to end the wretched run of debutant quarterbacks against this Macdonald defense. By no means will it be an easy task – even with Leonard Williams absent – but Mendoza could make a real statement to the rest of the league about his future with a win on Sunday in Vegas.
